premises.text: Existing recommendation systems fail because they rely on strangers' reviews, average ratings that ignore personal taste, and widespread fake reviews
premises.evidence_span: all of these systems are dependent on giving you reviews and recommendations from strangers

premises.text: LiveStar surfaces high-quality recommendations from professional critics as a trusted source
premises.evidence_span: The first group are professional critics, people with genuine expertise

premises.text: Friends are a trusted recommendation source, aided by Q&A that reaches non-users via email/SMS/Facebook with easy pre-populated surveys
premises.evidence_span: The second group are your friends

premises.text: An algorithm finds people with the same taste and surfaces their recommendations
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar algorithmically measures your taste and then compares it to other people

premises.text: One app covers multiple categories including restaurants, menu items, music, and movies
premises.evidence_span: you can go to LiveStar for restaurants, what to eat when you're at the restaurant, what music to listen to, and what movie to watch

value.text: Fast, personalized, high-quality recommendations from critics, friends, and taste-alikes
value.evidence_span: give you access to high-quality reviews from trusted sources

causal_links.evidence_span: provides fast access to high quality sources across a range of common real world scenarios

notes: Three enumerated review failures folded as one problem set (§4.1.6). Critic/friend/taste-alike kept as separately asserted source mechanisms (distinct paths to trusted recs). Category coverage split as one-stop destination claim. Demo date narrative treated as illustration of the same product.
